summary: BifrOSt covers the core indexing path: an app can add, replace and delete its own searchable items, the shell keeps a bounded per-app index, and the system Search panel lists the items under Documents. It does not cover app-side queries and suggestions, index extensions and delegates, custom or person attributes, error reporting, or the Foundation models search tool.

gaps: No app-facing query API (CSSearchQuery, CSUserQuery) and no suggestions, so apps cannot search their own index or build a search field on it.
No index client delegate and no index extensions for on-demand regeneration (CSSearchableIndexDelegate, CSIndexExtensionRequestHandler, CSImportExtension).
No Foundation models search tool (SpotlightSearchTool and its pipeline types), so indexed content cannot be given to the on-device assistant as context.
No index descriptions or protection classes; the shell index is a single JSON file per app with oldest-first eviction at 1000 items.
The shell index does not acknowledge calls, so remoteConnectionError is never raised and the shell's own oldest-first eviction is not visible to the SDK ledger.
